subject: Performance validation & close timeline — FinEdge benchmarking roadmap
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@finedge.com>
Cc: procurement@finedge.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Performance validation & close timeline — draft roadmap

Elena —

Attaching a draft validation roadmap and the benchmarking harness config so we can align on methodology before finalizing the MAP and the close timeline. Key asks in the document:

- Benchmarks to capture: p50/p95 token latency, TTFT for cold vs warm KV cache, sustained throughput at target concurrencies (4, 8, 16), and peak throughput until backpressure.
- Workload shape: 60% short prompts (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64–256), 10% long (256–1024).
- Model variants: FP16 baseline + 8-bit quantized candidate (we'll call these rdlw-1.0-fp16 & rdlw-1.0-q8).
- Test harness: Redwood loadgen v2.1 (configs attached), steps to warm KV cache, and canonical prompt templates (in the harness).

Ask: please confirm whether FinEdge wants us to run these in your VPC (we can provision a canary runner) or you will run them and share raw output. Also confirm target close date — we were thinking two weeks from go-ahead (propose Dec 15).

Attachments: FinEdge_MAP_DRAFT.pdf, benchmark-harness-config.yaml

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance validation & close timeline — draft roadmap

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the plan and the attachments. We ran an initial pass in our staging environment using Locust-based runners and saw TTFT numbers ~25–35% higher than what your draft suggests at concurrency 8. I attached the raw TSV of our run (finedge-bench-output.tsv).

A few notes and questions:
- We used a different load generator (Locust) which may explain some variance — are your harness directives tied to a particular connection/keepalive behavior?
- We saw higher memory pressure when using the quantized variant; can you confirm the model binary and quantization recipe you used for the q8 candidate?
- CompetitorX v2 was used as a reference point in our internal evaluation — can Redwood run a head-to-head using the same prompt templates so we can compare apples-to-apples?

We can either share access to a staging VPC for you to execute the run or we can keep iterating on our side and share outputs. Procurement is copied because we want to lock commercial terms once performance is agreed. Can you do a reproduction within 48 hours and share a short write-up?

Regards,
Elena Soto
Head of Infrastructure, FinEdge
Attachments: finedge-bench-output.tsv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance validation & close timeline — triage plan proposal

Tessa / Marissa —

I looked through Elena's TSV and the harness config. Proposed triage steps (short checklist attached):

1) Reproduce Locust run locally against our internal canary endpoint using the same prompt mix and tokenization. Owner: Marissa. ETA: 24 hours.
2) Verify model binaries: confirm fp16 vs q8 weights, quantization recipe, and kernel selection used by Redwood runtime. Owner: Sergio. ETA: 24 hours.
3) Run identical-config runs in FinEdge staging (if they provide creds) to rule out network/connection differences (keepalive, TLS handshake overhead). Owner: Marissa + Sergio. ETA: 48 hours after creds.
4) Align on measurement definitions (TTFT vs first-token latency vs overall request latency). Document both and always report p50/p95/p99 plus sample size. Owner: Karthik.
5) Competitor parity: define exact prompt template and tokenizer. Redwood will run CompetitorX v2 under same templates to provide an apples-to-apples comparison. Owner: Karthik / Marissa. ETA: 72 hours.

Notes: differences between load-generators (Locust vs Redwood loadgen) often stem from connection reuse semantics and default batching behavior. Also ensure KV cache warmup (we recommend 50 warmup requests per model shard) before measuring TTFT.

Attaching triage-checklist.md with explicit commands and expected output formats.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Performance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: triage-checklist.md

Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance validation & close timeline — next steps and checkpoints

Elena —

Appreciate the quick run and the TSV. Proposed plan to move forward:

1) Short smoke runs: Marissa will reproduce Locust config against our internal canary and share baseline numbers by EOD tomorrow (Dec 4).
2) Credentials: Sergio will coordinate a scoped FinEdge staging credential for a canary run (no production data). We only need VPC peering + a runner with SSH access. Sergio — can you confirm scope by EOD?
3) Competitor head-to-head: we'll run CompetitorX v2 with your prompt templates so we can present an apples-to-apples table.
4) Close timeline: assuming the above completes on schedule, proposed contract close target is Dec 15 (commercial to confirm). Checkpoint meeting: Dec 7 @ 10:00 PT to review preliminary numbers and any regressions.

I'll loop in Commercial for final pricing/credit asks after we have aligned on methodology.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
